ar.why: P1-026: one word for a meetup's chat, which the catalogue calls محادثة اللقاء. دردشة reads as idle chatter and شات is a loanword, and a member who meets two names for one panel looks for two features.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the event participants build in, spelled as the announcement (#294) spells it; one spelling, so a search for it finds every page.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a hackathon team, as the announcement says (انضمّ إلى فريق); طاقم reads as a crew or staff, which a team of participants is not.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the team member who manages it (invites, requests, submitting); كابتن is a loanword and رئيس suggests an office the product does not give.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a team's submitted project, as in the announcement's آخر أجل لتسليم المشاريع; إيداع reads as a bank deposit or a filing.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): one member of لجنة التحكيم, the jury the announcement names; قاضي is a judge in court.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): what participants build toward, as in مسار للمصادر المفتوحة; تراك is a loanword.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the criteria judges score against; روبريك is a loanword and سلم التنقيط reads as a school marking scale.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a judge stepping aside from an entry they have a conflict with; انسحاب is what a participant does when leaving a hackathon, a different act.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the approved organisation that runs a hackathon, never a single person; المنظّمين in the meetup terms names hosts and stays.

fr.why: P1-026: one word for a meetup's chat, « Discussion » in its panel and its entry. Chat is a cat in French and tchat is slang, and messagerie names an inbox of private messages, which the chat is not.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): spelled as the announcement (#294) spells it; hackaton is a common misspelling.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a hackathon team, as the announcement says; the English word is avoided in French copy.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the team member who manages it; leader is English and chef suggests authority over the others, which the role does not give.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a team's submitted project, as in Fin des dépôts; soumission also means submissiveness.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the panel that scores entries, and juré for one of its members, as the announcement says; un juge sits in a court.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): what participants build toward, as in un parcours open source; the English word is avoided in French copy.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the criteria judges score against; rubrique is a false friend meaning a section or column.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a juror stepping aside from an entry they have a conflict with; désistement is a participant leaving, a different act.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the approved organisation that runs a hackathon; organiseur is a desk organiser.

en.why: P1-026: one word for a meetup's chat, as its panel and its entry name it. A discussion reads as a forum thread, a different feature the product does not have.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): one spelling, as the announcement (#294) has it, so a search finds every page.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a hackathon team; squad is slang the rest of the copy does not use.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the member who manages the team (invites, requests, submitting); lead suggests authority over the others, which the role does not give.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): what a team submits by the deadline; an entry also means a registration, and the product keeps the two apart.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a member of the panel that scores entries, as the announcement says (judges you know by name).
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): what participants build toward, as in an open-source track; a theme is a look of the site.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the criteria judges score against, one word on every page.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): a judge stepping aside from an entry they have a conflict with; withdrawing is what a participant does when leaving a hackathon.
B-I18N-01 (Stage B): the approved organisation that runs a hackathon, spelled the British way as the plan and the rest of Stage B are.
